# hyperfluid_environment (Resource)

An environment: the space other resources are created in, through its `id`.

~> Destroying an environment deletes every resource in it. While `deletion_protection` is true, both destroying it and any change that replaces it (`name`, `slug`) fail.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "hyperfluid_environment" "analytics" {
  name = "Analytics"
  slug = "analytics"

  # Destroying or replacing the environment deletes everything in it.
  # Set this to false and apply before you mean to.
  deletion_protection = true
}

resource "hyperfluid_bucket" "lake" {
  env  = hyperfluid_environment.analytics.id
  name = "data-lake"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Display name, 3 to 63 characters. Changing this forces a new environment.
- `slug` (String) Slug: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. It is the import id. Changing this forces a new environment.

### Optional

- `deletion_protection` (Boolean) Refuse to destroy or replace the environment. Defaults to true; Terraform-only, never sent to the platform.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Environment id, the value other resources take as `env`.
- `namespace` (String) Kubernetes namespace the environment's workloads run in.
- `owner_id` (String) Id of the user who owns the environment, or null.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Environment import id is its slug.
terraform import hyperfluid_environment.analytics analytics
```
